reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as a produced comedy or creator video centered on an Instagram support call. Although a support character claims to control the account within the dialogue, the video does not show viewers being asked to pay, provide credentials, visit a destination, or participate in that mechanism. Its description and end card promote the creator's ordinary social presence and other videos, separate from the fictional support interaction.

citations.quote: Shot by: Taylor Nored & Randy Koszela Directed/Edited by: Lu Louis
Instagram Support! This is Titi!
I locked his d.m. so none of them hoes can message him no more
I made his profile picture your wedding photo permanently
I unfollowed the last three girls he follows

opening.argument: Judge, consider the exchange as a model of an unusually easy account fix. A caller brings a relationship problem to someone answering as Instagram support, and the response is framed as immediate account-level intervention: locked messages, a permanent profile-photo change, and unfollows. The caller's thanks supplies the payoff. The suggested action is to bring a problem to support; the promised benefit is control over someone else's account without any stated verification. There is no evidence that a viewer actually takes that step, but the sequence makes the service look available and effective.

citations.quote: Instagram Support! This is Titi!
I locked his d.m. so none of them hoes can message him no more. And then, I made his profile picture your wedding photo permanently.
Thank you. Really, thank you.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The production credits establish that the scene was made for a video; they do not, by themselves, resolve what impression its support exchange conveys. Nor is a payment or credential request necessary to notice the appeal of the claimed fix. The defense rightly points to the absence of a viewer-facing instruction, but the caller's gratitude follows a concrete claim of account control, not merely general advice.

citations.quote: Shot by: Taylor Nored & Randy Koszela Directed/Edited by: Lu Louis
I locked his d.m. so none of them hoes can message him no more
Thank you. Really, thank you.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The proposed link is between two characters in a scripted exchange, not between an offer and an action requested of viewers. The opening supplies no viewer instruction to obtain the claimed fix, and the account changes are claims in dialogue, not demonstrated results. The production credits and the character's exaggerated promise support an entertainment reading; the creator's description directs attention to social accounts and other videos, not an account-repair service.

citations.quote: Shot by: Taylor Nored & Randy Koszela Directed/Edited by: Lu Louis
I made his profile picture your wedding photo permanently
WATCH MY OTHER VIDS!

opening.argument: The concerning signal is the breadth of the claimed access. The speaker identifies as Instagram support, then says she locked a man's messages, permanently changed his profile picture, and unfollowed accounts for him. None of those claims includes his consent or a verification step. The account holder is not the caller in the dispute as described. A judge should give weight to how effortlessly the exchange presents access to a third party's account, even though it never shows the underlying controls being used.

citations.quote: Instagram Support! This is Titi!
my husband's Instagram feed is full of a bunch of thirst trapping insta hoes and he keeps liking all of their pictures.
I locked his d.m. so none of them hoes can message him no more. And then, I made his profile picture your wedding photo permanently.
I unfollowed the last three girls he follows.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this a comedy exchange and notes that no credentials or payment are requested. Those omissions limit what can be concluded, but they do not erase the specific access claims. The speaker describes changing messages, a profile photo, and follows on the absent account holder's behalf. The question is whether presenting that power as routine is a meaningful risk signal, even without an on-screen transaction.

citations.quote: I locked his d.m. so none of them hoes can message him no more
I made his profile picture your wedding photo permanently
I unfollowed the last three girls he follows.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Unusual access claims in a character's dialogue are not evidence that access was obtained, or that viewers were offered it. The same conversation begins with the support character saying the platform is not liable for users' behavior, then veers into personal insults and relationship advice. Those turns make the account-control claims part of an exaggerated sketch, while the supplied material identifies no route for viewers to request such changes.

citations.quote: here in Instagram we're not liable for what the users do on the platform.
Girl for what? Because this this is above your pay grade.
I locked his d.m. so none of them hoes can message him no more

opening.argument: This is not just a private fictional call left on its own: the video packages a support character who claims to solve the caller's problem, then the surrounding description directs viewers to the creator's Instagram and asks them to subscribe. That pairing gives the character's extraordinary account fix a promotional setting and a path to keep engaging with its creator. It does not explicitly offer viewers the same fix, but the support premise and the audience-facing calls to action should be considered together rather than treating the conversation and promotion as wholly unrelated.

citations.quote: INSTAGRAM SUPPORT FEAT. @BLAMEITONKWAY

Keep up with me! :mobile phone with arrow: INSTAGRAM: https://www.instagram.com/missamandaparis

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense separates the creator's social links from the fictional support interaction. That is a plausible reading, but the description does actively ask viewers to follow the creator after presenting the support character as a hero. The promotional context therefore deserves attention. Still, the defense is correct that neither the Instagram link nor the subscription request says viewers can obtain account changes.

citations.quote: She's the hero we deserve.
Keep up with me! :mobile phone with arrow: INSTAGRAM: https://www.instagram.com/missamandaparis
PLEASE SUBSCRIBE!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Following a creator and subscribing to a channel are ordinary promotion of entertainment content. The description also lists production credits and other videos; it never connects those actions to the character's claimed ability to alter an account. The opening's promotional setting is real, but its crucial offer-action link is inferred rather than stated or shown. The account fix remains an event in the dialogue, not a service proposed to viewers.
